clue.text: Magazine content making one proud?

parts.note: Punch was a famous British humour magazine, so being content in the manner of that magazine is a whimsical way of describing great delight

explanation.surface: A question about whether reading a magazine's articles can make someone proud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' reads as a noun (what the magazine contains) but is the adjective meaning happy; PUNCH was a long-running British satirical weekly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone extremely delighted, which is close to feeling proud and gratified.

clue.text: Calmness in crisis as men-friends cope amazingly

indicators.note: amazingly suggests the letters of men-friends cope are thrown into an astonishing new order

explanation.surface: A group of male friends handle a crisis with surprising ease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amazingly' rearranges the fourteen letters of MEN-FRIENDS COPE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the ability to stay cool and act sensibly when an emergency strikes.

clue.text: Theatre dipped into capital to mount The Mikado

indicators.note: in a down entry, mounting means the built word is read upwards, from bottom to top
dipped into means one word goes inside another word here

parts.note: Rome is the capital city of Italy
rep is short for repertory theatre

explanation.surface: A theatre company ventures into a capital city to stage Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dipped into' puts the theatre inside the capital, and 'to mount' reads the result upwards in this down entry. The surface makes The Mikado an operetta; here it is the title of Japan's ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mikado was the historical title used for the hereditary monarch of Japan.

clue.text: Broke using rocks

explanation.surface: Out of money, someone resorts to rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom stony broke means penniless, and something full of rocks or stones is described with the same adjective.

clue.text: People scattered since river dried up all around

indicators.note: all around means one word encircles the other pieces in this clue
in a down entry, up means this word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: something dried is arid
as can mean since, as in 'as it was late'
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: A population disperses because the local river has run completely dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the word for dried to read DIRA, and 'all around' wraps that round the other two pieces. 'dried up' looks like one phrase, but its two words do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: The term is used for a community dispersed far from its ancestral homeland.

clue.text: Back English novelist

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A call to support an English novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurence STERNE wrote Tristram Shandy. 'Back' looks like a verb meaning support but is the noun for a ship's rear.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne was the eighteenth-century author of Tristram Shandy, so he is an example of a writer of fiction.

clue.text: Investment one must have faith in

parts.note: a unit is a single thing, one
to trust is to have faith in

explanation.surface: Advice that a particular investment is one you must believe in.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit trust is a pooled fund in which savers buy shares, a common type of financial holding.

clue.text: It's excessive to be locked in prison house

indicators.note: to be locked in means one piece sits inside another, just as a prisoner sits in a cell

parts.note: a cage is a place of confinement, a prison
OTT is short for over the top, meaning excessive

explanation.surface: Someone protests that being jailed in a prison house is too harsh.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT is British shorthand for 'over the top'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottage is a small dwelling, a kind of home.

clue.text: High-level meeting at which opponents may be on toast?

definitions.text: High-level meeting at which opponents may be on toast?

parts.words: High-level meeting at which opponents may be on toast?
parts.note: describes a high-powered business meeting held over a morning meal, with the joke that rivals might be served up on toast

explanation.surface: Executives meet over the morning meal, and rivals may end up served on toast.
explanation.walkthrough: To have someone 'on toast' is a British idiom for having them at your mercy, so the toast is both breakfast and defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a meeting of important business people held early over the morning meal.

clue.text: Pressure to stop, say, a rumour about agent's job

indicators.note: to stop means this letter plugs a gap inside the other letters, as a stopper does
about here signals that the pieces before it are turned round and read backwards

parts.note: eg (for example) means say
noise can mean rumour or talk, as in 'there is noise about a takeover'
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Someone applies pressure to silence a rumour about an agent's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the three pieces before it to read ESIONAGE, and 'to stop' plugs the pressure letter into that after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Spying is the business of a secret operative, so it is the work a spy does.

clue.text: Popular couple parted completely

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a couple is two

explanation.surface: A celebrity couple have split up for good.
explanation.definitionFit: Something broken or cut into halves is divided entirely.

clue.text: Obviously, class must leave in good time

indicators.note: must leave means these letters depart from the longer word

parts.note: clearly means obviously
CL is an abbreviation for class

explanation.surface: Clearly, the pupils need to go home before it gets late.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving ahead of schedule is to be on time with room to spare.

clue.text: Gain insight into writer's French and criticise

parts.note: a pen is a writer, the tool that writes
et is French for and
to rate can mean to scold or criticise

explanation.surface: A writer's ambition to understand French culture and critique it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French and' gives ET, French for 'and'; 'rate' in the old sense of scold.
explanation.definitionFit: To see through to the heart of something is to understand it fully.

clue.text: Not a crude attempt to get set of supporters

indicators.note: not here instructs that the following letter is removed from the word

parts.note: coarse means crude
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Something described as a careful effort, not a rough one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a' removes the A from COARSE. The supporters are undergarments.
explanation.definitionFit: Corsets and similar foundation garments support the body, and the trade name covers them collectively.

clue.text: I help reds insidiously into senior post

indicators.note: insidiously suggests the letters of I help reds are worked into a sly new arrangement

explanation.surface: A political schemer helps communists creep stealthily into a senior position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'insidiously' rearranges I HELP REDS; 'into' links fodder and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder holds a position of seniority in a church or community, and the office is so named.

clue.text: Newbolt's old ship or boat each may visit

indicators.note: may visit means one piece pops in to stay inside the other

parts.note: sub is short for submarine, a boat
per means each, as in 'a pound per head'

explanation.surface: An old ship from a poem, or a boat that each traveller might go aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Henry Newbolt wrote the poem 'The Old Superb', about a ship of the line.
explanation.definitionFit: HMS Superb was the warship celebrated in Henry Newbolt's poem about the old vessel.

clue.text: Make firm accept damaged film

parts.note: do can mean make, as in 'do a cake'

indicators.note: accept means the firm takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
torn means damaged

explanation.surface: A company is forced to take on damaged goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dr. No' is the first James Bond film. 'Make firm' looks like 'make solid', but 'firm' is the company.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr. No (1962) was the first James Bond movie, an example of a motion picture.

clue.text: Skinny thing cross getting greeting in verse

indicators.note: in means the cross and the greeting sit inside the verse

parts.note: an ode is a lyrical poem, verse
X is the shape of a cross
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: An irritable person is greeted in a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skinny' looks like a thin person but means a thing made of skin; 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The skin of a bull or bullock is a thing made of skin, hence skinny in a playful sense.

clue.text: Hotel is remarkably unfriendly

indicators.note: remarkably suggests the letters of hotel is are rearranged in a striking way

explanation.surface: A hotel turns out to be strikingly unwelcoming.
explanation.definitionFit: Antagonistic and unwelcoming behaviour is opposed and unfriendly.

clue.text: The end of one University course

definitions.text: The end of one University course

parts.words: The end of one University course
parts.note: the annual Oxford and Cambridge Boat Race on the Thames finishes at a riverside district of west London

explanation.surface: What happens at the conclusion of a degree programme.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'course' is not a degree but the Boat Race course between Putney and a district of southwest London.
explanation.definitionFit: The finishing line of the Varsity Boat Race lies at this Thames-side district of London.

clue.text: In the drink, partner a swimmer

parts.note: ale is a drink, a type of beer
a wife is a partner in marriage

explanation.surface: Someone in the drink with their partner is a swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the drink' sounds like being in the water; 'drink' just gives ALE. The swimmer is a fish, a North American herring.
explanation.definitionFit: The fish is a herring of the North Atlantic coast, so it is a creature that swims.

clue.text: Reindeer found in Jordan? Certainly

indicators.note: found in means the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Asked whether reindeer live in Jordan, someone answers yes.
explanation.walkthrough: Dancer is one of Santa's reindeer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dancer is one of Santa Claus's sleigh-pulling team in the traditional poem.

clue.text: Offender is racist, men determined

indicators.note: determined here means the letters of racist men are resolved into a fixed new order

explanation.surface: Determined racist men are labelled offenders.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer or villain is one who commits offences.

clue.text: Half of Dickens' work is dreary

indicators.note: half of means only the opening portion of the title is used

parts.note: ... House is a novel by Charles Dickens

explanation.surface: A verdict that half of what Dickens wrote is dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Desolate and cheerless, the adjective describes something bleak and depressing.

clue.text: Animal to purchase, say — kid

indicators.note: say means the word is spoken and written as it sounds

parts.note: to buy is to purchase
a son is a kid, a child

explanation.surface: Buying an animal, say, for a child.
explanation.definitionFit: The bison is a large wild ox, so it is a beast.

clue.text: Heard no animal call

indicators.note: heard means the word that follows is spoken, so its sound matters

parts.note: nay means no

explanation.surface: No animal call was heard.
explanation.definitionFit: The sound a horse makes is a familiar animal cry.

clue.text: Believer's name put forward, a fellow-poet close to Dante

indicators.note: put forward means this letter is shifted earlier in the word

parts.note: a Christian is a believer

explanation.surface: A believer's name is put forward as a poet close to Dante.
explanation.walkthrough: 'name' gives N, moved one place forward. Dante here is Dante Gabriel Rossetti, the brother of poet Christina Rossetti, not Dante Alighieri.
explanation.definitionFit: Christina Rossetti was a Victorian poet and the sister of the painter-poet Dante Gabriel Rossetti.

clue.text: Small expense making occupant of mill very pained?

parts.note: a peppercorn is what fills a pepper mill
rent means torn apart, as a heart in great pain

explanation.surface: A tiny cost leaves the contents of a pepper mill feeling hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: A peppercorn rent is a nominal sum charged to keep a lease legal.
explanation.definitionFit: A token charge, nominal and minimal, is a trivial cost.
